overview.title: What is Atlas Island?
overview.text: Atlas Island is an international community of liberty-minded people building toward a network of voluntary, sovereign floating settlements on the ocean. Founded in 2022 by Seasteading Institute ambassadors, the project follows a phased five-stage plan from online community building to full maritime sovereignty in international waters. The name comes from Ayn Rand's Atlas Shrugged, and the central idea is that members can "vote with their boat" - choosing which platform community to join or leave rather than being subject to a single government.

overview.title: Who joins Atlas Island?
overview.text: Atlas Island draws classical liberals, libertarians, and anarcho-capitalists who are committed to the non-aggression principle and private property rights. Members come from all walks of life - most are currently land-based, while some are already living aboard vessels in marinas around the world. The community is primarily based in the Americas and Europe, connected through a global Telegram group and mailing list. The founders describe it as open to anyone who believes in individual sovereignty and opposes coercive governance.

history.text:
Atlas Island was founded in January 2022 by Mason and Ryota Sekine, two Seasteading Institute ambassadors who concluded that existing seasteading projects were trying to do too much at once. Rather than targeting large floating structures in international waters from the start, they developed a phased approach that begins with building an online community and grows incrementally toward the ocean.

Mason, an emergency physician with an engineering background, describes his role as custodian rather than owner - the goal from the start was a community-driven organization rather than a top-down project. Ryota Sekine, a healthcare startup founder based in Chicago with Japanese heritage, co-founded the project with the same pragmatic outlook. The about page notes a board of directors and advisors have since joined.

The project distinguishes itself from earlier seasteading efforts by focusing on what can be done within existing legal frameworks, starting with marinas near metropolitan areas before eventually moving into international waters. Vessels operate under flags of convenience, similar to cruise ships, for maritime legal protection.

milestones.detail: January 2022 by Seasteading Institute ambassadors Mason and Ryota Sekine

milestones.label: Stage I Launched
milestones.detail: Online community established via Telegram group (t.me/atlasisland) and mailing list

milestones.label: 600 Members
milestones.detail: Approximately 600 members across Telegram and mailing list as of mid-2025, primarily from the Americas and Europe

milestones.label: LiberArx 64 Unveiled
milestones.detail: Purpose-built solar catamaran presale launched at Free Cities Conference in Prague, Oct-Nov 2025

milestones.label: Stage II Scouting
milestones.detail: Identifying marina locations in the Mediterranean and Caribbean for first physical communities

location:
Atlas Island currently operates as a global online community, with physical locations being identified for Stage II. The first physical focus area is Florida, where several existing members already live aboard vessels in local marinas.

For Stage II marina communities, the founders are targeting one location in the Mediterranean and one in the Caribbean, with a third location in Oceania listed as lower priority. The exact sites are under negotiation, with the aim of co-locating within upcoming Free Cities projects.

The long-term vision for Stages III through V involves moving communities progressively further offshore - first to protected harbor waters, then to coastal positions 5-10 nautical miles out, and finally into international waters where platforms would operate as independent Free Cities under flags of convenience.
duration:
Atlas Island is not a fixed-length program. Stage I membership in the online community is open-ended - members join and participate indefinitely as the project advances toward physical communities.

The founders estimate the full arc from online community to established ocean-based settlements will span 10 to 20 years, based on comparisons to the development timelines of other Free Cities projects. There are no cohort start dates, application seasons, or minimum commitment periods at any stage.
pricing:
Joining the Atlas Island online community during Stage I is free. Members apply via the website and are added to the Telegram group and mailing list at no cost.

Stage II will require members to acquire a floating vessel. Co-founder Mason has designed the LiberArx, a purpose-built solar catamaran that went to presale in late 2025, with deliveries targeted by end of 2026. Visit [liberarx.com](https://liberarx.com) for current presale details. Ongoing marina and docking costs during Stage II are separate and depend on the specific marina location.

howToEnter.text: Prospective members apply via the form on the Atlas Island website. After completing the application, members are invited into the Telegram group at [t.me/atlasisland](https://t.me/atlasisland), the primary hub for community discussion and project updates. The about page notes that prospective residents must affirm a commitment to the non-aggression principle and individual sovereignty - those who believe in centralized government control are directed to find another organization.

faqs.question: What is Atlas Island?
faqs.answer: Atlas Island is an international community building a network of voluntary, floating settlements for liberty-minded people. It follows a five-stage plan from online community to full ocean sovereignty. The community is currently in Stage I and operates as a global online network.

faqs.question: Who can join Atlas Island?
faqs.answer: Anyone who commits to the non-aggression principle and values individual sovereignty is welcome. The community is especially geared toward classical liberals, libertarians, and anarcho-capitalists. Most current members are land-based; some are already living aboard vessels in marinas around the world.

faqs.question: How do I join Atlas Island?
faqs.answer: Complete the application form at [atlasisland.org](https://atlasisland.org/) and join the Telegram community at [t.me/atlasisland](https://t.me/atlasisland). Stage I membership costs nothing.

faqs.question: What stage is Atlas Island currently in?
faqs.answer: As of mid-2025, Atlas Island is in Stage I - the online community building phase. The founders are actively recruiting members and scouting marina locations in the Mediterranean and Caribbean for Stage II.

faqs.question: Where will Atlas Island be located?
faqs.answer: The first physical communities (Stage II) are planned as marina-based networks near metropolitan areas. Priority locations are being sought in the Mediterranean and Caribbean, with Florida as the initial focus area. Stages III through V would move communities progressively further offshore, ending in international waters.

faqs.question: What is the five-stage development plan?
faqs.answer: Stage I is the current online community. Stage II involves members acquiring vessels and docking in marinas near cities. Stage III moves vessels to protected harbor waters with floating infrastructure added. Stage IV establishes offshore platforms 5-10 nautical miles from shore. Stage V is full ocean sovereignty in international waters as independent Free Cities.

faqs.question: What is the LiberArx and how does it relate to Atlas Island?
faqs.answer: The LiberArx is a purpose-built solar catamaran designed by Atlas Island co-founder Mason as a practical floating home for seasteaders. It is comparable in living space to a 2-3 bedroom apartment and includes electric motors, a large solar array, and is designed for comfort as a primary residence. A presale was launched at the Free Cities Conference in Prague in late 2025, with deliveries targeted by end of 2026. See [liberarx.com](https://liberarx.com) for current details.

faqs.question: Do I need to own a boat to join Atlas Island?
faqs.answer: No - Stage I membership requires only an internet connection. Vessel ownership becomes relevant at Stage II, when members begin living aboard in marina communities. Most current members are land-based and do not yet own vessels.

faqs.question: What are Atlas Island's core principles?
faqs.answer: Atlas Island is built on the non-aggression principle: members agree not to initiate force against others and uphold private property rights. The community opposes coercive governance and taxation. The concept of 'voting with your boat' - the freedom to leave any platform at any time - is central to its governance philosophy.

faqs.question: When will physical marina communities open?
faqs.answer: The founders are currently negotiating marina locations in the Mediterranean and Caribbean for Stage II. No confirmed opening dates have been announced as of this update. The full project spans an estimated 10 to 20 years from Stage I to ocean sovereignty.

faqs.question: How many people are in the Atlas Island community?
faqs.answer: As of mid-2025, Atlas Island had approximately 600 members across its Telegram group and mailing list, primarily based in the Americas and Europe. Several members are already living aboard vessels in marinas globally.

faqs.question: What governance model does Atlas Island use?
faqs.answer: Atlas Island envisions a decentralized model of independent local clubs, similar to yacht clubs, operating within a shared philosophical framework. In future stages, competing private providers would operate platforms, and members retain full freedom to move between them. This ensures accountability through mobility rather than majority-vote politics.
